leads.candidate: The couple banyan trees (雙夫妻樹) at 228 Peace Memorial Park's Fude Temple
leads.reason: Four large banyan trees (Ficus microcarpa), described consistently across multiple WebSearch summaries as over 100 years old, standing beside Fude Temple (福德宮) inside 228 Peace Memorial Park, central Zhongzheng District -- right pair has dense aerial roots ('male'), left pair has none ('female'), locally called 'shuang fuqi shu' (double couple trees) and a minor pilgrimage spot for romance blessings. This reads as a strong candidate: free public park in the city centre, a compact named ensemble with one obvious place to stand (in front of the temple), genuinely old. NOT delivered as verified because every source repeating these specific facts (tree count, aerial-root sexing, the '百年' age claim) traces back to blog.xuite.net (specifically nicecasio/twblog/104402467), which is unreachable from this environment (DNS: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND blog.xuite.net) -- per the rule that a WebSearch AI summary is a lead and never a source, these facts were never confirmed on a directly fetched page. Wikipedia's own article on the temple (zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/二二八公園福德宮, fetched directly) covers the temple's history and deities in detail but does not mention trees at all. parks.gov.taipei (the city's own park guide, which turned up in search results) and crgis.rchss.sinica.edu.tw (Academia Sinica's temple GIS database) both looked like they would settle it but were unreachable (connection refused / DNS failure) within this pass's timeout budget.
leads.next_step: A future pass with different network access, or a browser session, should try: (1) blog.xuite.net/nicecasio/twblog/104402467 directly, (2) parks.gov.taipei's 228 Peace Memorial Park page (parks.gov.taipei/parks/m2/pkl_parks_m2C.php?sid=374), (3) the temple's own Facebook page (facebook.com/228fudetemple), or (4) a fresh WebSearch that surfaces a reachable news article rather than the xuite blog. If confirmed, this is very likely a four-tree ensemble worth shipping alongside tpe_001 through tpe_004.

host_notes: blog.xuite.net: DNS resolution fails outright (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) on every URL tried, both curl and WebFetch. Cost: the 228 Park banyan lead above could not be confirmed because of this single host.

crgis.rchss.sinica.edu.tw: DNS resolution fails (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). Academia Sinica's temple/cultural-resources GIS database, would have been a useful independent source for temple-adjacent trees generally, not only 228 Park.

guide.cc.ntu.edu.tw: connection refused (ECONNREFUSED) on NTU's own official campus building guide, which would have given a cleaner primary source for the Geology Building's ginkgo/dawn redwood than the blog used instead.
parks.gov.taipei / parks.taipei: connection refused (ECONNREFUSED). Taipei's own official parks department site; would be a good source for any city park's named trees generically, worth retrying.
blog.udn.com: 403 Forbidden to WebFetch on all paths tried (multiple posts about the NTU ginkgo). udn's blog platform generally blocks plain fetchers; unknown workaround this pass.

eculturedata.gov.taipei/api/site/module/tree: returns {"status":403,"error":"權限不足"} (insufficient permission) to plain curl -- this is the backing API for the official Protected Trees Information Platform (受保護樹木資訊平臺, eculture.gov.taipei/trees), which otherwise renders individual tree records fine when fetched by direct /tree/{id} URL (e.g. eculture.gov.taipei/trees/zh-tw/tree/3220 worked and returned a full record: species, address, girth, health status). The search/list/filter endpoints did not yield working results from this environment (data.taipei's dataset download API also 404'd/errored on several attempts at the underlying CSV/JSON for the protected-trees dataset). A session that can find the right ID for a given landmark (e.g. via a working search interface or a browser session) can pull a clean official record per tree; blind guessing IDs is not practical.

data.taipei (dataset d9d1140b-c2c3-405f-8dd1-7b87b00f6f53 / older ref 121274, '臺北市受保護樹木'): the download API returned a Slim Application Error and an empty resourceAquire response on every path tried; the bulk protected-trees CSV/JSON could not be retrieved this pass despite the dataset clearly existing (referenced by multiple third-party writeups). Worth a retry, ideally from a session that can browse data.taipei's UI directly, since a working bulk export would upgrade this whole city from web-research to register-backed and is exactly the kind of thing rung 5 (register import) should chase separately from this verification pass.
